expertise: Current diff impact and semantic disposition review
Source contract authority and conditional-rule review
Control-plane evidence handoff and semantic governance review

ballot_rationales.rationale: The requirement is scoped by this Skill's use and anti-use contract to a real extensibility decision. It asks for current consumer variation, distinct change reasons, ownership, and likely evolution before abstraction, and explicitly prefers direct code or configuration when variation is unproven. That is professionally correct, actionable, and properly placed as a High-Value Rule; it mandates evidence rather than a universal extension mechanism.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: When extensibility-design is selected for a real extension decision, current consumer variation, distinct change reasons, ownership, and likely evolution must justify abstraction; otherwise direct code or configuration remains the preferred outcome.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Retain the explicit no-extension fallback and reopen this disposition if the source or detector context changes, especially if the rule begins prescribing plugins or hooks without verified variation.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The rule is professionally correct and actionable: before introducing an extension abstraction it requires named consumers, distinct change reasons, ownership, and likely evolution, and it prescribes direct code or configuration when variation remains unproven or locally owned. Its placement under extensibility-design High-Value Rules and the Registry Trigger bounds it to an actual task-local extension decision. It does not impose trust or rollback mechanisms universally: adjacent source rules condition origin, authenticity, or integrity controls on executables crossing install or update trust boundaries, authenticated metadata on existing update channels, and rehearsed last-known-good rollback on mutable or consequential activation; config-only and static extensions instead require evidence-backed non-applicability.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies when extensibility-design evaluates a proposed extension point, plugin, policy hook, configuration variation, or other shared variation boundary. It does not apply when no task-local extensibility decision exists. Executable trust controls apply only when artifacts cross install or update trust boundaries; update-metadata authentication applies to an existing update channel; rollback proof applies when activation is mutable or consequential. Config-only or static extensions may establish inspected, evidence-backed non-applicability.
ballot_rationales.decision_owner: The assigned extensibility-design analysis-agent or review-agent owns the variation-evidence decision; the relevant host, policy, or threat-model authority owns disputed executable trust, update-channel, activation, and rollback conditions.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep the variation in direct code or configuration until current consumers, independent change reasons, ownership, and likely evolution support a stable extension boundary. Record inspected evidence for any inapplicable trust, update, or rollback control, and escalate unclear ownership, trust or tenant crossings, corrupting failure, unavailable isolation, or unproved last-known-good recovery.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Valid contextual rule. In this Skill, the requirement is scoped to deciding whether proven variation warrants an abstraction; the same rule names the evidence an agent must collect and the direct-code or configuration fallback when evidence is absent. It prevents speculative authority and compatibility surfaces rather than imposing an unconditional mechanism.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: extensibility-design owns this decision only when a task proposes an extension point, plugin, policy hook, or shared configuration boundary and claims independently evolving consumers.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Name current consumers, distinct change reasons, ownership, and likely evolution; keep the variation in direct code or configuration and escalate unresolved ownership until that evidence supports a narrow extension contract.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The requirement is bounded by the preceding artifact-trust rule and Stop Conditions: executable installation or update paths need selected trust proof, mutable or consequential activation needs recovery, and config-only or static extensions may claim non-applicability only with inspected evidence. Requiring a concise rationale prevents silent control omission, is actionable, and belongs in Stop Conditions because failure to substantiate non-applicability blocks closure rather than imposing every control universally.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: When an assigned extensibility review decides that a named trust, update, isolation, recovery, or retirement control is not triggered, current inspected source evidence and a concise rationale must support that non-applicability.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep the rule adjacent to the explicit escalation conditions and conditional artifact-control rule; reopen the disposition if surrounding triggers change or non-applicability can be asserted without inspected evidence.

ballot_rationales.rationale: This is a valid contextual evidence gate, not an unconditional implementation mechanism. Its placement in Stop Conditions governs a claim that a particular control is inapplicable and makes that claim actionable by requiring a concise rationale tied to inspected evidence. The surrounding source supplies the non-applicability boundaries: executable origin, authenticity, or integrity applies only across install or update trust boundaries; authenticated metadata applies to existing update channels; last-known-good rollback applies to mutable or consequential activation; config-only or static extensions may document why those controls do not apply. Requiring evidence prevents silent omission without making every control mandatory.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies only when an assigned reviewer or analyst concludes that a control named by extensibility-design is inapplicable to the current extension boundary. It does not apply when the Skill itself is out of scope because no extensibility decision exists. A non-applicability claim must identify the control, its trigger, and inspected facts showing the trigger is absent; where trust, update, tenant, consequence, or rollback conditions are unclear, the source requires escalation rather than waiver.
ballot_rationales.decision_owner: The assigned extensibility-design analysis-agent or review-agent owns the documented applicability assessment; the relevant host, policy, threat-model, or operational owner confirms disputed trust, update, consequence, and rollback facts.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Record the evaluated control, trigger condition, inspected evidence that the trigger is absent, residual risk, and residual owner. Do not claim non-applicability when an executable crosses a trust boundary, an existing update channel lacks authenticated metadata, or mutable or consequential activation lacks rehearsed last-known-good recovery; satisfy the control or escalate.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Valid contextual rule. The surrounding trust rule distinguishes executable or update boundaries and mutable or consequential activation from config-only or static cases. Requiring inspected evidence and rationale before declaring a listed control inapplicable preserves fail-closed trust, metadata authentication, and rollback behavior; absent evidence, the agent has a clear stop rather than permission to bypass a control.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: extensibility-design owns non-applicability only for a task-local extension control after inspecting artifact type, install or update trust boundary, update metadata channel, activation mutability, and failure consequence.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Do not waive origin, authenticity, integrity, authenticated update metadata, or rehearsed last-known-good rollback on assertion alone; retain the applicable control or escalate until inspected evidence supports non-applicability, and re-evaluate when those conditions change.

limitations: This majority is authoring lifecycle evidence only.
It cannot satisfy readability or professional-completeness formal attestations.
The record contains no generated single-source-of-truth disposition entries.
A rewrite majority requires a source edit before any resolved governance entry can exist.
